questions.question: Which method involves coating iron with a layer of zinc to protect it from rusting?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Galvanisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Galvanisation** is a metallurgical process where a protective **zinc coating** is applied to **iron** or **steel** to prevent **rusting** and **corrosion**.
 
• The most prevalent technique is **hot-dip galvanizing**, which involves immersing the metal components into a bath of **molten zinc** at temperatures typically around **450 °C**.
 
• The process works by providing **sacrificial protection**; because zinc is more **electrochemically active** than iron, it serves as an **anode** and corrodes first if the surface is damaged, sparing the underlying iron.
 
• When exposed to the atmosphere, the zinc reacts with **oxygen** to form **zinc oxide**, which then reacts with **carbon dioxide** to create a dull grey, fairly strong layer of **zinc carbonate** (ZnCO₃).
 
• This **carbonate layer** is insoluble in water and adheres tenaciously to the zinc, providing a stable **barrier** that prevents further **oxidation** of the base metal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electroplating**

 
 
• It uses **electrical current** to deposit a thin layer of metal, such as **chromium**, **nickel**, or **silver**, onto the surface of another metal.
 
• It is widely used in the **automobile industry** for aesthetics and to enhance **wear resistance** and **conductivity**.
 
 
 
• **Tinning**
 
 
• This involves coating iron or steel with a layer of **tin** (Sn).
 
• Since tin is **non-toxic** and resists **organic acids**, it is primarily used in the manufacturing of **food containers** (tin cans).
 
• Unlike zinc, tin only provides **barrier protection**; if the layer is scratched, the iron underneath will rust even faster.
 
 
 
• **Painting**
 
 
• This is a basic **barrier method** where a layer of paint prevents **moisture** and **oxygen** from reaching the metal surface.
 
• It is cost-effective for large structures like **bridges** and **ships** but requires frequent **re-application** as the paint layer degrades over time.

questions.question: Two lens of power (+ 4 D) and (- 6 D) are placed in contact with each other. What will be their combined focal length in cm?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**- 50 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When two or more **thin lenses** are placed in **physical contact** with each other coaxially, the total **optical power (P)** of the combination is equal to the **algebraic sum** of the individual powers of the lenses.
 
• The formula for the **equivalent power** is expressed as **P = P₁ + P₂**. In this specific case, the given powers are **P₁ = + 4 D** and **P₂ = − 6 D**.
 
• By substituting these values into the formula, the net power of the lens combination is calculated as **P = (+ 4) + (− 6) = − 2 D**.
 
• The **focal length (f)** of a lens system is mathematically defined as the **reciprocal of its power**. When the power is measured in **Dioptres (D)**, the focal length is initially calculated in **meters (m)** using the relation **f = 1 / P**.
 
• For the resultant power of **− 2 D**, the focal length in meters is **f = 1 / (− 2) = − 0.5 m**.
 
• To convert the focal length into **centimeters (cm)** as required by the question, the value in meters must be multiplied by **100**, leading to **− 0.5 × 100 = − 50 cm**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nature of Lens and Power**:

 
 
• A **convex lens** is known as a **converging lens** and is assigned a **positive power** because it brings parallel rays of light to a real focus.
 
• A **concave lens** is known as a **diverging lens** and is assigned a **negative power** because it causes parallel rays of light to spread out from a virtual focus.
 
• Since the resultant power in this calculation is **negative (− 2 D)**, the entire lens combination behaves effectively as a **single concave (diverging) lens** with a focal length of **50 cm**.
 
• The **S.I. unit** of power of a lens is the **Dioptre (D)**, where **1 D** is equivalent to the power of a lens whose focal length is exactly **1 meter**.

questions.question: The kinetic energy of an object of mass m moving with a velocity of 5 m/s is 25 J. If its velocity is doubled to 10 m/s, what will be its kinetic energy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**100 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kinetic Energy (K.E.)** is the energy an object possesses due to its **motion**. It is mathematically expressed by the formula K = (1)/(2)mv² , where **m** represents the **mass** of the object and **v** represents its **velocity**.
 
• Based on the initial conditions, the object has a **velocity (v₁)** of **5 m/s** and a **Kinetic Energy (K₁)** of **25 J**. By rearranging the formula to solve for mass: 25 = 1/2 × m × 5² → 25 = 1/2 × m × 25, which gives a **mass (m)** of **2 kg**.
 
• When the **velocity (v₂)** is doubled to **10 m/s**, the new kinetic energy is calculated using the same mass: K₂ = 1/2 × 2 × 10² = 1 × 100 = **100 J**.
 
• A fundamental property of this relationship is that **Kinetic Energy** is **directly proportional** to the **square of the velocity** (K ∝ v²). Since the velocity increased by a factor of **2** (from 5 to 10), the kinetic energy must increase by a factor of 2² = **4**. Therefore, 25 J × 4 = **100 J**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nature of Kinetic Energy**:

 
 
• It is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has magnitude but no specific direction.
 
• The **SI unit** is the **Joule (J)**, defined as **kg⋅m²/s²**.
 
• It can never be **negative** because mass is positive and the square of velocity is always non-negative.
 
• **Work-Energy Theorem**: It states that the **net work done** on an object results in a change in its **kinetic energy** (W = ΔK).
 
• **Momentum Relationship**: Kinetic energy can also be expressed in terms of **momentum (p)** as K = frac{p²}{2m} .

questions.question: An object is placed at infinity in front of a concave lens. The image formed will be _____________ .

options.text: Real, erect, and at the principal focus
Virtual, erect, and highly diminished at the focus

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Virtual, erect, and highly diminished at the focus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **concave lens** is known as a **diverging lens** because it bends parallel light rays outward after they pass through it.
 
• When an object is positioned at **infinity**, the rays of light hitting the lens are **parallel** to the **principal axis**.
 
• After **refraction**, these rays diverge and do not meet on the other side; however, when produced backward, they appear to meet at the **principal focus (F₁)**.
 
• The image formed is **virtual** because the light rays do not actually intersect, and **erect** because it maintains the same vertical orientation as the object.
 
• Since the rays appear to converge at a single point (the focus), the image is considered **highly diminished** or **point-sized**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Image Characteristics of Concave Lenses:**

 
 
• Regardless of the position of the object, a **concave lens** always forms a **virtual, erect, and diminished** image.
 
• The **magnification (m)** for a concave lens is always positive and **less than 1**.
 
• These lenses are used to correct **Myopia** (near-sightedness) as they help diverge light before it reaches the eye.
 
 
 
• **Lens Formula and Sign Convention:**
 
 
• The relationship between focal length (f), object distance (u), and image distance (v) is given by the formula: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u .
 
• According to the **Cartesian sign convention**, the **focal length** of a concave lens is always **negative**.
 
• A **convex lens**, by contrast, can form both **real** and **virtual** images depending on the distance of the object from the optical center.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why humans have the highest concentration of harmful chemicals in their bodies?

options.text: They are exposed to chemicals through air and water
They occupy the top trophic level in food chains
They consume more pesticides directly than other organisms
They eat large quantities of contaminated animal products

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They occupy the top trophic level in food chains**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phenomenon responsible for this occurrence is **Biological Magnification** (or **Biomagnification**), which refers to the progressive increase in the concentration of harmful chemicals at each higher **trophic level**.
 
• Many agricultural chemicals, such as **pesticides** (e.g., **DDT**) and **industrial wastes**, are **non-biodegradable**, meaning they cannot be broken down by biological processes or excreted by organisms.
 
• These chemicals enter the food chain at the **producer level** (plants) via soil or water and are transferred to consumers as they feed on the organisms from the level below.
 
• Since **humans** generally occupy the **topmost trophic level** in most food chains, they consume a large volume of biomass from lower levels, leading to the **maximum accumulation** of these toxins in their bodies over time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trophic Levels:**

 
 
• These represent the functional steps in a **food chain** or **food web**, beginning with **autotrophs** (producers) and ending with **apex predators**.
 
• While energy decreases by 90 percent at each step (the **10 percent law**), non-biodegradable substances do not dissipate, causing their concentration to spike as the total biomass of the level decreases.
 
 
 
• **Bioaccumulation vs. Biomagnification:**
 
 
• **Bioaccumulation** refers to the buildup of a substance within a single organism's body over its lifetime.
 
• **Biomagnification** refers to the increase in concentration as the substance moves through the entire **ecosystem** from one level to the next.
 
 
 
• **Health Impacts:** High concentrations of **heavy metals** and **synthetic chemicals** in humans can lead to **carcinogenic effects**, **reproductive issues**, and damage to the **nervous system**.

questions.question: Unbalanced forces acting on an object always cause _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Change in motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **unbalanced force** is defined as a situation where the **net force** acting on an object is **non-zero**, meaning the individual forces do not cancel each other out.
 
• According to **Newton's Second Law of Motion**, the **acceleration** of an object is produced when an **unbalanced force** acts upon it; this is mathematically represented as **Force = mass × acceleration**.
 
• Because **acceleration** involves a **change in velocity**, the application of an unbalanced force must result in a **change in motion**, which can manifest as a change in **speed**, a change in **direction**, or both.
 
• If an object is **stationary**, an unbalanced force will cause it to start moving; if it is already **moving**, the force will cause it to **speed up**, **slow down**, or **turn**.
 
• Unlike **balanced forces**, which maintain an object's current state of **equilibrium**, unbalanced forces are the primary cause of **mechanical work** and **kinetic energy** variation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Balanced Forces**:

 
 
• These occur when the **resultant force** is exactly **zero Newtons**.
 
• An object under balanced forces follows **Newton's First Law**, remaining at **rest** or continuing at a **constant velocity**.
 
 
 
• **Mass**:
 
 
• In **Newtonian physics**, **mass** is a measure of **inertia** and remains **constant** regardless of the external forces applied.
 
• Forces affect the **motion** of the mass but do not **increase or decrease** the quantity of matter itself.
 
 
 
• **Inertia**:
 
 
• This is the **inherent property** of matter that **resists** changes in its state of motion.
 
• The **magnitude** of the unbalanced force required to change motion is directly proportional to the **inertia** (mass) of the object.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the 'Indus Water Treaty' signed between India and Pakistan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1960**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indus Water Treaty (IWT)** is a major water-sharing agreement signed on **September 19, 1960**, between the **Government of India** and the **Government of Pakistan**.
 
• The treaty was brokered by the **World Bank**, which was then known as the **International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)**, after nearly a decade of negotiations.
 
• The historic document was signed in **Karachi** by the then Indian Prime Minister **Jawaharlal Nehru** and the then Pakistani President **Ayub Khan**.
 
• It remains one of the most successful transboundary water treaties in the world, having survived multiple conflicts and wars between the two neighboring nations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **River Allocation and Distribution**:

 
 
• The treaty divided the six rivers of the **Indus Basin** into two distinct groups: the **Eastern Rivers** and the **Western Rivers**.
 
• **Eastern Rivers**: India was given exclusive rights over the waters of the **Ravi**, **Beas**, and **Sutlej**.
 
• **Western Rivers**: Pakistan was allocated the waters of the **Indus**, **Jhelum**, and **Chenab**. However, India maintains certain limited rights on these rivers for **non-consumptive use**, such as **run-of-the-river** hydroelectric power plants, irrigation, and domestic consumption.
 
 
 
• **Implementation and Dispute Resolution**:
 
 
• The **Permanent Indus Commission (PIC)** was established as a bilateral body to monitor the implementation of the treaty and manage technical data exchange.
 
• The commission consists of high-ranking **Commissioners** from both countries who are required to meet at least once a year.
 
• The treaty outlines a three-step dispute resolution mechanism involving **Questions** (handled by the Commission), **Differences** (handled by a **Neutral Expert**), and **Disputes** (referred to a **Court of Arbitration**).

questions.question: The Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF) was established in India in which of the following years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1995-96**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF)** was established by the **Government of India** in the financial year **1995-96**.
 
• The fund was created with the primary objective of providing **low-cost developmental loans** to **State Governments** and **Union Territories** for financing various rural infrastructure projects.
 
• The **National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)** is the official agency responsible for managing and maintaining the RIDF.
 
• The resources for the fund are mobilized from the shortfall in **Priority Sector Lending (PSL)** targets of **Scheduled Commercial Banks** operating in India.
 
• The initial corpus for the first tranche of the fund (**RIDF I**) was **Rs. 2,000 crore**, which has been progressively increased through annual **Union Budget** allocations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development)**:

 
 
• It was established on **July 12, 1982**, following the recommendations of the **B. Sivaraman Committee** (CRAFICARD).
 
• It acts as the apex regulatory body for the overall regulation of **Regional Rural Banks (RRBs)** and **Apex Cooperative Banks** in India.
 
 
 
• **Scope of RIDF Projects**:
 
 
• Currently, there are **39 eligible activities** categorized under three broad sectors: **Agriculture and Allied Sectors**, **Social Sector**, and **Rural Connectivity**.
 
• Key eligible projects include **minor irrigation**, **soil conservation**, **rural drinking water supply**, **primary school buildings**, and **rural roads**.
 
 
 
• **Financing and Repayment Terms**:
 
 
• The loans sanctioned under RIDF are repayable within a period of **7 years**, which includes a **grace period** of **2 years**.
 
• The interest rates on these loans are usually linked to the **Bank Rate** prevailing at the time of sanction by the **Reserve Bank of India**.

questions.question: In India, which of the following is NOT considered as a constitutional body?
Which of the following amendments to the Indian Constitution is regarded as a major milestone in the country’s taxation system for introducing the Goods and Services Tax (GST)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**101st Amendment, 2016**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016**, is the landmark legislation that facilitated the implementation of the **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**, a comprehensive **indirect tax** on the manufacture, sale, and consumption of goods and services throughout India.
 
• This amendment introduced **Article 246A**, which conferred concurrent powers upon both the **Parliament** and the **State Legislatures** to legislate on taxes relating to goods and services.
 
• It also led to the insertion of **Article 279A**, mandating the constitution of the **GST Council** within sixty days of the commencement of the act to oversee the tax administration and policy.
 
• The primary objective was to eliminate the **cascading effect** of taxes (tax on tax) and replace multiple levies like **Excise Duty**, **Service Tax**, **VAT**, and **Entry Tax** with a single unified structure.
 
• Following the ratification by more than half of the State Legislatures, the GST regime was officially launched across the country on **July 1, 2017**, under the principle of **One Nation, One Tax**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **86th Amendment Act, 2002**:

 
 
• This amendment made **Education** a Fundamental Right for children between 6 and 14 years by inserting **Article 21A**.
 
• It also added a new **Fundamental Duty** under **Article 51A(k)** for parents or guardians to provide educational opportunities.
 
 
 
• **100th Amendment Act, 2015**:
 
 
• This act gave effect to the acquiring of certain territories by India and transfer of certain other territories to **Bangladesh**.
 
• It ratified the **Land Boundary Agreement (LBA)** signed between the two nations to resolve long-standing border disputes involving **enclaves**.
 
 
 
• **97th Amendment Act, 2011**:
 
 
• It provided constitutional status and protection to **cooperative societies**.
 
• The amendment included the right to form cooperatives as a **Fundamental Right** under **Article 19(1)(c)** and added **Article 43B** to the **Directive Principles of State Policy**.

questions.question: Indigenous GSAT-7R weighs 4400 kg, making it the heaviest communication satellite launched from which country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **GSAT-7R** is an advanced, indigenous communication satellite developed by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** primarily for the **Indian Navy**.
 
• With a mass of approximately **4400 kg**, it represents a significant milestone in the domestic production of high-throughput satellites within **India**.
 
• The satellite is designed to replace the aging **GSAT-7** (Rukmini) and is intended to provide secure, real-time communication for maritime assets.
 
• The development and launch of a satellite in this weight class underscore **India**'s self-reliance in space technology and its ability to manufacture heavy-duty payloads.
 
• It utilizes multiple frequency bands, including **UHF**, **S-band**, **C-band**, and **Ku-band**, to facilitate network-centric warfare capabilities for the **Indian Armed Forces**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **GSAT Series Evolution**:

 
 
• **GSAT-7**: Launched in **2013**, it was the first dedicated multi-band communication satellite for the **Indian Navy** to monitor the **Indian Ocean Region**.
 
• **GSAT-7A**: Known as the 'Angry Bird', it was launched in **2018** to provide connectivity for the **Indian Air Force**.
 
• **GSAT-7B**: A dedicated satellite approved for the **Indian Army** to enhance tactical communication.
 
 
 
• **Launch Vehicle Capability**:
 
 
• The launch of satellites weighing over **4000 kg** is typically handled by the **Launch Vehicle Mark 3 (LVM3)**, formerly known as **GSLV Mk III**.
 
• Before the **LVM3** became operational, **India** often relied on the **European Space Agency's** **Ariane 5** rocket from **French Guiana** for such heavy payloads.
 
• The transition to launching **4400 kg** satellites from Indian soil marks a strategic shift in **ISRO**'s heavy-lift capabilities.

questions.question: Which of the following is the highest peak of the Western Ghats mountain range?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anaimudi, Anamalai Hills**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anaimudi** is the highest peak in the **Western Ghats** and is widely recognized as the highest point in **South India**.
 
• It stands at an elevation of **2,695 meters** (8,842 feet) and is located in the **Idukki district** of **Kerala**.
 
• The peak is strategically situated at the junction of three major mountain ranges: the **Anamalai Hills** to the north, the **Palani Hills** to the northeast, and the **Cardamom Hills** to the south.
 
• The name **Anaimudi** literally translates to **Elephant's forehead** in **Malayalam** and **Tamil**, referring to the mountain's resemblance to an elephant's head.
